content.content:
The user asks: Identify the presidents of the United States who served two terms and their respective political affiliations. Need to list all US presidents who served two full terms (i.e., elected twice). Provide political party affiliation. Likely include: Washington (no party), Jefferson (Democratic-Republican), Madison (Democratic-Republican), Monroe (Democratic-Republican), Jackson (Democratic), Van Buren? No, Van Buren served one term. Lincoln (Republican) served one term (though re-elected). Actually Lincoln served one term and was assassinated early second term, but he was elected twice? He was elected 1860 and 1864, so served two terms (though second term cut short). So include him. Grant (Republican) served two terms. Cleveland served non-consecutive, not two consecutive terms; still served two terms but not back-to-back. He served two terms (non-consecutive) but qualifies as served two terms? The question likely about presidents who served two terms (any two terms). So include Cleveland (Democrat). Wilson (Democratic) two terms. Harding? No. Roosevelt (FDR) four terms. Eisenhower two terms. Kennedy one term. Johnson one term (partial). Nixon resigned. Ford one. Carter one. Reagan two terms. Bush Sr two terms. Clinton two terms. Bush Jr one term. Obama two terms. Trump one term. Biden currently one term.

Also earlier presidents: John Adams one term, Thomas Jefferson two terms, James Madison two, James Monroe two, Andrew Jackson two, Ulysses S. Grant two, Grover Cleveland two (non-consecutive), Woodrow Wilson two, Dwight D. Eisenhower two, Ronald Reagan two, Bill Clinton two, George W. Bush two, Barack Obama two.

Also include: Washington (no party). Also maybe John Quincy Adams one term. James K. Polk one.

Also include: William McKinley was assassinated early second term, but elected twice. He served one full term and part of second. He counts as two-term elected president? Typically two-term presidents list includes those elected to two terms, even if didn't complete second. So include McKinley (Republican). Theodore Roosevelt succeeded McKinley and then elected one term. Not two.

Also include: William Howard Taft one. So list:

- George Washington (No party / Independent)
- Thomas Jefferson (Democratic-Republican)
- James Madison (Democratic-Republican)
- James Monroe (Democratic-Republican)
- Andrew Jackson (Democratic)
- Abraham Lincoln (Republican) (served two terms, second cut short)
- Ulysses S. Grant (Republican)
- Grover Cleveland (Democratic) (non-consecutive)
- Woodrow Wilson (Democratic)
- Dwight D. Eisenhower (Republican)
- Ronald Reagan (Republican)
- Bill Clinton (Democratic)
- George H. W. Bush (Republican)
- Barack Obama (Democratic)

Also include: William McKinley (Republican). He was assassinated early second term, but served two terms elected. Usually two-term list includes McKinley? I think typical "two-term presidents" includes those who were elected to two terms, regardless of completion. Many lists exclude McKinley because he didn't complete second term, but still considered two-term. The user didn't specify "full terms". Provide clarity.

Also include: Franklin D. Roosevelt (Democratic) served more than two terms, but includes two terms as part of four. Not needed.

Thus produce answer.

Will verify via Wikipedia.

content:
**U.S. Presidents who have been elected to (and served) two terms – with their political party affiliations**

| President | Years in Office (two terms) | Political Party* |
|-----------|----------------------------|------------------|
| **George Washington** | 1789‑1797 | No formal party (often described as *Independent*; later identified as a “Federalist‑leaning” figure) |
| **Thomas Jefferson** | 1801‑1809 | Democratic‑Republican |
| **James Madison** | 1809‑1817 | Democratic‑Republican |
| **James Monroe** | 1817‑1825 | Democratic‑Republican |
| **Andrew Jackson** | 1829‑1837 | Democratic |
| **Abraham Lincoln** | 1861‑1865* | Republican (re‑elected in 1864; assassinated early in his second term) |
| **Ulysses S. Grant** | 1869‑1877 | Republican |
| **Grover Cleveland** | 1885‑1889 & 1893‑1897 (non‑consecutive) | Democratic |
| **Woodrow Wilson** | 1913‑1921 | Democratic |
| **William McKinley** | 1897‑1901* | Republican (re‑elected in 1900; assassinated early in his second term) |
| **Dwight D. Eisenhower** | 1953‑1961 | Republican |
| **Ronald Reagan** | 1981‑1989 | Republican |
| **Bill Clinton** | 1993‑2001 | Democratic |
| **George H. W. Bush** | 1989‑1993 & 1993‑1997 | Republican |
| **Barack Obama** | 2009‑2017 | Democratic |

\* Both Lincoln and McKinley were assassinated before completing their second terms, but each had been **elected to a second term** and therefore count as two‑term presidents.

\* *Political Party* reflects the party with which the president was affiliated at the time of his elections. Early presidents (Washington, Jefferson, Madison, Monroe) belonged to the first party system; “Democratic‑Republican” was the dominant party of that era. Washington never joined a party, so he is listed as independent.

---

### Quick notes

- **Non‑consecutive terms** still count as two terms. Grover Cleveland is the only president with such a record (22nd and 24th president).  
- Presidents who served **more than two terms** (e.g., Franklin D. Roosevelt) are not listed here because the request was for those who served exactly two terms.  
- Presidents who served **only one term** (or less, due to death, resignation, or loss of re‑election) are omitted.  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like additional details such as major achievements, election margins, or a chronological timeline!
